### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **65** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/objects/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**90** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json adf6ee0948d8dd8e747678e6d5107e0c4a86bb31`.

⛔ **17** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/objects/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `isSystem (5 routes)`
- **3** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `VALIDATION_FAILED (literal, 42 pages)`, `organization_id (literal, 39 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 49 pages)`
- **15** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **221** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **179** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json adf6ee0948d8dd8e747678e6d5107e0c4a86bb31` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `32b206b3533a5f855b82fde15dd717ca31b9019a` — the merge of head `ac7e06d99504da19669bc6ce16643ee99c41a29d` into base `adf6ee0948d8dd8e747678e6d5107e0c4a86bb31`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 32b206b3533a5f855b82fde15dd717ca31b9019a && git checkout 32b206b3533a5f855b82fde15dd717ca31b9019a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin adf6ee0948d8dd8e747678e6d5107e0c4a86bb31 ac7e06d99504da19669bc6ce16643ee99c41a29d && git checkout -B drift-repro adf6ee0948d8dd8e747678e6d5107e0c4a86bb31 && git merge --no-ff ac7e06d99504da19669bc6ce16643ee99c41a29d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json adf6ee0948d8dd8e747678e6d5107e0c4a86bb31
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs adf6ee0948d8dd8e747678e6d5107e0c4a86bb31` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ac7e06d99504da19669bc6ce16643ee99c41a29d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/automation/assignment-rule.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts + packages/spec/scripts/liveness/empty-state-registry.mts (hunk 4, consented 6674042568), packages/objectql/src/assignment-rules.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/assignment-rule-hooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/objects/sys-assignment-rule.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-plugin.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts, scripts/platform-object-tenancy-census.json, the four platform-objects translation files, .changeset/30066-organization-assignment-rules.md (widened to the whole non-prose diff; the cited code on `main` — `engine-insert.ts` InsertFacet.assignment, `engine-hook-dispatch.ts`, `queue-hooks.ts`, plugin-security `grant-holder-membership-refusal.ts` and `security-plugin-write-tenant-wall.ts`, `sys-member.object.ts`, `sys-queue.object.ts`, `core/security/user-ban.ts`, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `packages/spec/liveness/*` — was read, not reviewed)

Governing text: ruling A 6631036940; execution parameters 6670178869 (items 1–8); claim 6672306838 with amendments 6672490095, 6673262187, 6674205693, 6674382817; dev report 6673979825; spec#3 consents 6672529419 (hunks 1–3, terms) and 6674042568 (hunk 4) on #30558; ADR-0142 D5 and merge question 11; the PR body. Read-only shape held: `git diff origin/main...head`, files via `git show`, the card and every comment, the head's check-runs through the API. PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.

**Check-runs on this head** (API, at review time): 64 runs, 55 `success`, 9 `skipped`, 0 red, 0 running — Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Type Check · consumer gates (the `check:app-nav-i18n` that was red at `ab98c3b8`), Lint · repo & tooling gates (census), every Test Core shard, the UI jobs. Landing precondition ② is met as read.

**The four `packages/spec` hunks against the consent terms, line by line.**

1. **Hunk 1, `kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts`** (+3 −2, comment lines only). The `[ADR-0142 D5]` comment above the `assignment_rule` entry changes exactly the clause "and declared only: organization-authored routing is deferred (merge question 11)" into "an organization authors its own as `sys_assignment_rule` rows, which the engine evaluates before these and which may not take a declared rule's name"; the `loadOrder: 17` sentence, the ledger sentence and "customized by a clone under a new name, never by an overlay" are kept. The entry line itself is diff context: `description: 'A rule a package declares to route new records to a queue or a person'`, `allowRuntimeCreate: false`, `supportsOverlay: false`, `allowEnvironmentOverlay: false`, `supportsVersioning: false`, `executionPinned: false`, `loadOrder: 17`, `domain: 'security'` — all untouched, as the consent requires (organization rules are rows, not items of this type). **Holds.**
2. **Hunk 2, `system/constants/platform-object-names.ts`** (+1). `'sys_assignment_rule'` under `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['plugin-sharing']`, between `'sys_assignment_cursor'` and `'sys_queue'`: sorted position, one line. **Same-commit term, verified on the commit API, not the body:** `4b6296e8` holds the object, `objects/index.ts`, `sharing-plugin.ts`, the hooks, the objectql seam and tests (10 files, no roster line); `d86cdc3e` holds the roster line, the inventory row, the census row and the changeset (4 files). The term's purpose — the line never lands ahead of the object — holds in this PR because `4b6296e8` precedes `d86cdc3e` on the branch and both merge together. Cost of the deviation: the three intermediate commits `4b6296e8`, `b0458ed8` and the pre-roster tree are not bisect-clean for `platform-object-names.test.ts` (the dev measured 1 failed / 13 passed without the line); a squash merge makes that moot. The seat accepted the split rather than a rewrite of pushed history; **judged acceptable**, named here as the consent asks.
3. **Hunk 3, `automation/assignment-rule.zod.ts`** (+14 −4, all inside the `AssignmentRuleSchema` docblock; the `lazySchema` opening line and every key, `.describe()` and refinement are diff context). The rewritten sentences checked one by one against `packages/objectql/src/assignment-rules.ts` at this head: "that organization's active rows first, ascending by `sort_order` and then by name" = `authoredRules` sorts `sortOrderOf(a) - sortOrderOf(b) || localeCompare(name)` and skips `active === false`; "the declared rules after them, in registry order" = `rules = [...own, ...fallback]`, `fallback` from `rulesFor` in `listRules()` order filtered by `switchedOn`; "across both, the first entry whose `criteria` match decides, and its target stands even when it does not resolve" = `assignOne` returns after the first `matches`, and `route` / `routeToUser` return on an unresolved queue, an empty pool or a lapsed user without trying the next rule; "When the organization's rows cannot be read, the row is written as it stood rather than routed by the declared rules alone" = `own === null → continue`; "may not take a declared rule's name" = the `declaredNames` skip with `warnOnce('shadowed::…')` plus the save guard; "A user target owns the row only while the user is an active member … logged once" = `routeToUser` on `answer === 'member'`, else `warnOnce('lapsed-user::rule::user::org')`; "an organization's row by its own `active`" = the `active` skip, the ledger read is declared-only. **Every sentence is what the code does, in the order the code does it.** Generated output: nothing under `packages/spec/generated`, `packages/spec/scripts` or `scripts/` renders this docblock (the only other carriers of the old sentence on `main` are the hand-written liveness ledger, see ③, and ADR-0142), so "regenerate, never hand-edit" has nothing to regenerate; the body's "gen:schema / gen:docs no diff" is consistent with that.
4. **Hunk 4, `scripts/liveness/empty-state-registry.mts`** (+8 −0, one object literal inserted directly after the `assignment-rule.zod.ts` / `criteria` entry). `file` names the object module, `property: 'criteria'`, `semantics: 'scope'`, the rationale carries the five points the consent listed (catch-all at the end of the organization's order; selects, grants nothing; only an ownerless, queue-less row; the author's target and the active-member rule for a user; failure direction is mis-routing among the author's own targets), evidence names `assignment-rules.ts` and the hooks file. Zero deletions, so every existing entry is byte-identical. The description it classifies ("leave it empty to take every new record that no earlier rule took") is what `matches` does for an absent `criteria`. "Spec property liveness" is green on this head. **Holds.**
5. **Nothing else under `packages/spec`**: the diff's file list has exactly these four paths there.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Roster (the schema face) widens.** `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_OBJECT_NAMES` / `isPlatformProvidedObjectName` answer true for one more real object; nothing accepted before is refused. `platform-object-names.test.ts` on `main` holds the roster to the declared `*.object.ts` set both ways, and the declaration is in this PR. **Right: widening, as declared.**
2. **The object is what ruling A and the parameters bind.** `sys-assignment-rule.object.ts`: `isSystem: true`, `managedBy: 'config'` (the `sys_queue` / `sys_sharing_rule` posture, compared on `main`), `organization_id` a required lookup to `sys_organization` (parameter 6: non-null, behind the wall), `name` unique per organization (`{ fields: ['name'], unique: 'organization' }`, the same index form `sys_queue` and `sys_sharing_rule` use), one entry per row (`object_name`, `criteria`, `sort_order`, `recipient_type` queue|user, `recipient_id` via the existing `recipient-picker` widget whose `dependsOn` sibling is literally `recipient_type`, `strategy`, `load`, `active`), a `by_object` list view sorted object → sort_order → name (the evaluation order). Census: `reach: in`, `tenantField: organization_id`, totals 93→94 registered, 47→48 in reach, out-of-reach unchanged. Inventory: `fate: 'attribution'`, `PMAIN`, no anchors, the row shape of `sys_assignment_cursor` above it. Setup nav `nav_assignment_rules` beside `nav_queue_members`, `requiresObject`, `requiredPermissions: ['manage_platform_settings']`, opening the generic record list (the purpose-built page is the `domain:ui` card). **Right.**
3. **Evaluation order (parameter 1).** `apply` reads the organization's rows once per organization in the batch (`authored` map), orders them, then `[...own, ...fallback]`, first match. The reason given in the code and the docblock — the activation ledger is one deployment-wide row with no organization column, so an organization cannot switch a package rule off for itself, and package-first would let it never win — matches `switchedOn` on `main`. Pinned by "an organization rule wins over a declared rule that also matches; an unmatched row falls back" and by the dev's ablation (order swapped → 3 failed). **Right.**
4. **User target (parameter 2).** Save: the guard asks `organizationMemberStanding` and refuses `not_member` / `unconfirmable` (`reference_not_found`) and `banned` (`reference_user_banned`); a membership read that throws refuses the save with the reason rather than storing an unjudged target. Insert: `routeToUser` writes `owner_id` only on `member`, otherwise ownerless with one `warn` per (rule, user, organization); the insert is never refused; a throwing read leaves the row as it stood. "Active member" = a `sys_member` row for (user, organization) and `isUserBanInForce(user)` false — `sys_member` on `main` has no status column (fields: id, display_title, created_at, organization_id, user_id, role), so there is no membership state the predicate overlooks; it agrees with plugin-security's `holdsMembership` (one `sys_member` find under `{ isSystem, tenantId: organizationId }`) and adds core's one ban predicate (`core/security/user-ban.ts`). **Right.**
5. **Lapsed queue (parameter 3)** — `route` is unchanged from `main` for a queue target: unresolved → ownerless, no queue, warn once; empty pool → park, warn once; strategy read failure → park. **Unchanged, as the parameter says.**
6. **Names (parameter 4).** The guard refuses a name any declared rule holds (`registry.listItems('assignment_rule')`, switched on or off, any object), and the evaluator independently skips such a row with a warn and never evaluates it, so a declaration installed after the row was written also wins (ADR-0131 D4, one namespace) and the boot report says so at `error`, naming the organization. Cursor rows are keyed (rule, entry = rule, organization), so an authored rule's rotation can never share a cursor with a declared rule's. **Right.**
7. **Criteria / load (parameter 5).** `assignmentExpressionRefusals` compiles `criteria` by `ExpressionEngine.compile` (what `matches` evaluates with) and `load` by `compileCelToFilter(load, { variables: {} })` (what `leastLoaded` lowers with); the guard adds whatever `AssignmentRuleSchema.safeParse` refuses for the one-entry shape (strategy on a user target, `least_loaded` without `load`, `load` without the strategy, a non-machine queue name, an unknown recipient type), mapped to the row's columns by `columnOf`. A rule the seam could not evaluate is refused when written. **Right.**
8. **Tenancy (parameter 6).** The row: `organization_id` required and indexed; the wall of `security-plugin-write-tenant-wall.ts` (ADR-0105 D5 / ADR-0123 D2) stamps an insert's organization from the active one and refuses a new row landing in an organization the caller lacks, so a tenant admin authors into their own organization and the guard's membership check runs against the organization the row actually lands in (`present(row.organization_id) ?? session.organizationId`). Reach: `authoredRules` reads `{ object_name, organization_id: the row's organization }` under a context pinned to that organization; a queue target is resolved by `resolveQueue(name, organizationId)` in the row's organization; a user target must be that organization's member. **A rule written in organization A cannot route a row of organization B, reach a queue authored in B, or hand a row to a user who is not a member of the row's organization**; a platform administrator (wall-exempt) may author into any organization, which is the existing posture of `sys_queue`. Permission to author: the same as `sys_queue` / `sys_sharing_rule` on `main` (`isSystem`, `managedBy: 'config'`, Setup behind `manage_platform_settings`); no new door. Cross-org pin: "routes … only for the organization that authored it" (`other.queue` and `other.owner_id` null).
9. **The engine call site** (`engine.ts`, one line + comment): `evaluator.mayRoute(object)` replaces the non-empty `rulesFor(object)` test. `mayRoute` = declared rule names the object, or (`object !== 'sys_assignment_rule'` and the table is registered and `carriesQueueColumn(schema)`) — registry reads only. The candidate's organization is the row's own column, else the active organization, else the derived one — unchanged. `engine-insert.ts` is untouched (the `InsertFacet.assignment` host adapter already exposes `listRules`, and a `find` whose `limit` the rule read leaves unset; `engine-find.ts` gives `limit` no default at the query layer, so an organization's rule list is read whole). **Right.**
10. **Cost.** For an object with the queue column while the table is registered: one `sys_assignment_rule` find per organization in the batch, plus for a user target one `sys_member` find and one `sys_user` find per (user, organization) memoised per pass. Without the table, or for an object without the column, nothing is read (pinned "the cheap path"). **As the body states.**
11. **Boot report.** `reportShadowedAuthoredAssignmentRules` is awaited at `kernel:ready` beside `reportShadowedAuthoredQueues`, same shape (`engine.find` with `context: SYSTEM_CTX`, which the engine honours through `mergeReadContext(query.context, options.context)`), logs at `error` when the logger has one, stands down with no declared rule or no table. Bound regardless of `enforce`, inside its own try/catch. **Right.**
12. **`@objectstack/objectql` public surface.** `src/index.ts` gains `ASSIGNMENT_RULE_OBJECT`, `assignmentExpressionRefusals`, `organizationMemberStanding` and the type `OrganizationMemberStanding`; nothing removed; `OWNERSHIP_QUEUE_SOURCE_SLOT` stays unexported. **Widening, covered by the minor.** `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` gains `SysAssignmentRule` and the five guard exports. **Widening.** `@objectstack/platform-objects`: four nav labels, no export change.
13. **The declared-rule behaviour change** — see ③.2; the accept set does not move.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/30066-organization-assignment-rules.md`: `minor` for `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`. No `major` (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, pre-GA). Level axis (ruling A as `clause2-line.mjs` states it): `Metadata-protocol: added` needs at least one package whose published source moves `minor` or above — spec (roster, docblock, registry comment) and objectql do; only a declared `none` forces `patch`, so the `minor` on platform-objects for four nav labels and on cli for an inventory row are admissible under `added`, and all five sit in the one `fixed` group, so the per-package level touches the CHANGELOG heading and nothing of the version. **Check Changeset** concluded `success` on this head.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` are byte-identical in the PR body and the changeset, and match the claim's expectation and the consent's terms. `Fixes #30066` is in the body.
- `Skills-docs:` grammar `follow-up owed — FILES` is the declared one; the body's line names the same two files as the changeset's (`content/docs/automation/queues-and-assignment-rules.mdx`, `skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md`) but adds a parenthetical after each, so the two lines are not byte-identical. No script reads the line (the only hit under `scripts/` and `.github/` is a comment), the seat rewrites `owed — FILES` to `#N` at ACCEPT anyway. **Should-fix, prose.** The grep term of the consent is met: `skills/**` on this head carries no "deferred" / "declared only" reading about assignment rules (re-run here, no hit).

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions: []` in the dev report. The dev's eight deviations and the body's acceptance notes, each answered:

1. **Placement in `plugin-sharing`, call site `engine.ts`** — accepted in amendment 6672490095; the object sits beside `sys_queue` / `sys_queue_member` / `sys_assignment_cursor` whose model it follows (ADR-0142 names plugin-sharing the owner package of the queue tables), and the one-line call-site change is in the insert body `engine.ts` still hosts. **Accepted.**
2. **Behaviour change for declared rules.** On `main` a declared entry `assignTo: { type: 'user', value }` wrote `owner_id = value` unconditionally; at this head it assigns only where that user is a `sys_member` of the row's organization and not banned, else ownerless with one warn. The accept set is unchanged (the entry still parses, loads and is evaluated; nothing is refused at load or save), so this is not a `no (narrowing)` case on the schema face; it is a change in what an accepted input does at runtime. It is what execution parameter 2 says ("at insert time a target that no longer resolves is handled like a lapsed queue … Today the engine writes the owner without resolving it"), agreed by the maintainer, and the ADR already held a declared user id to resolution at load and `os lint` warns on it (`assignment-rule-user-target`). The changeset's Upgrading paragraph states it. **Open question for the maintainer, does not block:** a declared user-target rule in a deployment whose users carry no `sys_member` rows (a store seeded by hand, or `admin-import-users` without memberships) assigns nothing from this release; is `Metadata-protocol: added` the intended reading, or should the record carry `semantic` beside it? Both grade `minor`, so the gates are indifferent; the seat should name it at ACCEPT.
3. **Commit split** — ①/hunk 2 above. **Accepted.**
4. **Translations held for #30512** — plugin-sharing's `i18n-extract.config.ts` lists its objects explicitly and does not name `SysAssignmentRule`, so `check:i18n` is green and the object's labels wait for the rebase; the four nav labels (amendment 6674382817) ride here because `check:app-nav-i18n` reads the nav id only after the runtime merge, and each sits under `nav_queue_members` in en, es-ES, ja-JP, zh-CN. **Accepted.**
5. **Two checks beyond the ruling** — an object that does not exist or has no queue column is refused at save (the seam's `rulesFor` would warn and route nothing; refusing at authoring time is the louder failure the card's 防错 axis asked for), and the boot report at `error` names a shadowed row an administrator has to rename. Both are mechanism around the ruled behaviour, neither widens or narrows a spec. **Accepted.**
6. **Harness attribution line and the PR body's first line** — reported, not a conflict. **Noted.**
7. **Repo-wide `pnpm lint` run by the dev** — reported, no conflict of substance. **Noted.**
8. **Subscribed to the PR's activity** — the harness default; landing stays the seat's. **Noted.**

Author note: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no outside author.

**Transitional text.** ADR-0142 merge question 11 and the D5 note still say "deferred" on `main`; execution parameter 7 puts that rewording in its own Tier H `docs/adr` PR, so the spec comment and the ADR disagree until it lands. Intended by the parameters; the seat tracks the ADR PR.

### ④ Design judgment

1. **Hunk 1 against its consumer.** The registry entry is read by the metadata API and Studio to refuse runtime creation of `assignment_rule` items (`allowRuntimeCreate: false`), and that refusal is still right: an organization's rule is a `sys_assignment_rule` row, not a registry item, so the measured 403 on `PUT /api/v1/meta/assignment_rule/…` stays and the comment now says where the other door is. **Holds.**
2. **Hunk 2 against its consumer.** The roster test and the object land together; the inventory test ("a platform object without a row reds here, by name") is satisfied by the row; the census check ran in the green "Lint · repo & tooling gates". No generated artifact derives from the roster. **Holds.**
3. **Hunk 3 against the ruling and the code** — ① hunk 3 above: every sentence names a branch of `apply` / `authoredRules` / `assignOne` / `route` / `routeToUser` at this head, in the order they run. The docblock is the one place an author of a declared rule learns that an organization's rows go first, so stating the order here is what the consent asked for and what the card's "Not measured" item deferred to execution. **Holds.**
4. **Hunk 4 against its gate.** `check:empty-state` walks the object's permissive empty states; the entry classifies the one `criteria` has and the gate is green on this head. The rationale's claims are true of the code: `matches` returns true on an absent `criteria`, the seam routes only a row with no owner and no queue, the save guard holds the user target to membership. **Holds.**
5. **The guard against the engine's hook contract.** `beforeUpdate` receives `previous` as the row's pre-image (`engine-hook-dispatch.ts`, the per-row dispatch), so the merged-row judgement is on real data; the patch-touches-a-judged-column test means an administrator can always flip `active` or relabel a rule whose target lapsed, which is the remedy the warn names. The guard's `engine.find(o, { where, context, limit })` form is the one `queue-hooks.ts` and plugin-security's `holdsMembership` use, and the engine merges `query.context` with `options.context`, so the membership read runs as system pinned to the organization. Re-binding unregisters by package id first (pinned "re-binding replaces, never stacks"). **Holds.**
